interpretation: These cold-start results qualify the exact checkpoint-storage recipes, image initialization, checkpoint payload and restore software together; they are not generic snapshot-technology speed measurements.
Documented disk limits provide a plausible storage constraint to investigate later, but do not establish saturation or quantify how much restore time is storage-limited.
Flush duration is directly measured in the retained capture receipt. No block-device bandwidth, cache state, I/O queue depth, or per-stage restore I/O profile was collected by this check.
Slower restore under these recipes does not imply BIR is intrinsically slower, nor predict results on larger, different, or local storage.
The Boltz2 evaluation model-cache RWX filesystem is separate from its RWO checkpoint PVC; do not conflate them.
No changes, extra I/O benchmark, infrastructure cost mutation, causal forensic expansion or peer evidence edits.
